races.title: State Assembly, District 3
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dom Belza
cands.bio: Agricultural businessman and realtor from a fourth-generation Yuba County family. He has worked 19 years buying and selling agricultural and commercial property. He served on the Marysville City Council and founded the conservative political action committee Free California. Republican candidate for Assembly District 3.

endorsements.text: International Union of Operating Engineers (IUOE) Local 3 and Reform California, as listed by Ballotpedia.
Campaign site shows endorsement quotes from James Gallagher, Rep. Kevin Kiley, and retired Sen. Jim Nielsen.

In his Ballotpedia survey he lists California Republican Assembly, Sutter and Placer County Republican Parties, Cal Fire Local 2881, and Police Officers Research Association of California (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Dom Belza was born, where he grew up, or when his family settled in the area beyond his statement that they arrived in 1906. We found no independent reporting on his time on the Marysville City Council, and no record of what he did there on housing, growth, taxes, data centers, or other issues. We found no stated position from him on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, abortion, or school choice. His statements on guns, immigration, and public safety come only from his own campaign materials. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he will fight to protect the Second Amendment and criticizes the Legislature for passing laws he says infringe on gun rights.

workers-first.evidence: Says he supports ending sanctuary laws, better enforcement, and President Trump's border actions, and wants to secure the border against illegal immigration.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he supports stronger penalties for repeat offenders and more support and resources for peace officers, and that he was Honorary Co-Chair of the Prop 36 campaign.

cands.name: James "Jamie" Johansson
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 3 in 2026. Ballotpedia lists him as also known as Jamie. He placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 29.3% of the vote and advanced to the November general election against fellow Republican Dom Belza.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to California. We found no record of his jobs, business history or any elected offices, so his fit for the job is not rated. We found no documented actions or stated positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or schools. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and the only page available had no biography or campaign themes. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.
